evidence: app/package.json:9 — next pinned to 16.4.3, the current stable release (confirmed via nextjs.org changelog, 16.4.3 published 2026-10-23)
app/next.config.mjs:1-3 — config is empty: no cacheComponents, no experimental flags, no PPR, no unstable_*
app/app/layout.tsx:1-2 — imports only Link and Metadata, both long-stable App Router APIs
app/components/MovesSection.tsx:4 — useRouter from next/navigation, stable since Next 13
app/components/HomeBrowser.tsx:2 — only useMemo/useState/useEffect from React 19.3.1 (stable since Dec 2024), no canary hooks (no useOptimistic/useActionState/use cache anywhere)
grep across app/ — zero matches for unstable_, experimental_, use cache, cacheComponents, generateStaticParams, PPR
reach.rationale: The app's entire framework surface is Link, Metadata, useRouter, route segment configs and plain React hooks — all long-stable. Static analysis also reports zero experimental markers and no config flags. This is the far end of the conservative scale: it neither risks experimental breakage nor samples any of Next 16's newer directions.

evidence: app/next.config.mjs:2 — empty config object: no experimental opt-ins anywhere in the repo
app/app/layout.tsx:5-7 — the only caching directives live as route segment exports colocated with each route file, easily findable and swappable
app/lib/api.ts:9-16 — the single API_BASE_URL origin and in-memory cache live in one module, so no framework behavior leaks across files
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain. The one piece of framework policy that touches many files (the no-cache segment configs) is a two-line, mechanical, uniform pattern per route, and the data layer is funneled through a single lib/api.ts module.

evidence: SPEC.md:36-40 — spec explicitly demands data fetched over HTTP at request time, never prerendered or embedded at build time, and the app honors it with app/app/layout.tsx:5-7 (force-dynamic/revalidate=0/force-no-store) plus app/lib/api.ts:26 (cache: 'no-store')
app/app/[...slug]/page.tsx:4-5 — same stable segment-config pattern used for the catch-all 404 route, consistent with the rest
app/lib/api.ts:11-16 — hand-rolled promise-cache instead of any experimental framework cache API; plain fetch + Map, no unstable_cache/cacheLife/cacheScope
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used, and the conservative choices are each justified by a hard spec requirement (live API at request time). The author deliberately stayed on plain fetch and a hand-rolled cache rather than reaching for newer caching primitives.

findings.issue: The app is built entirely on the 'previous' caching model (dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache segment configs). As of Next 16.4, Cache Components is now recommended for every app and create-next-app enables it by default; it becomes the default in Next 17, where these segment configs are removed (confirmed in nextjs.org/docs route-segment-config version history and the 16.4 blog post). Stable today, but this is the legacy path with a known removal date.
findings.suggestion: Plan a migration to the Cache Components model (cacheComponents + partialPrefetching) when upgrading to Next 17; the data layer is already centralized in lib/api.ts, so the change is tractable.

findings.issue: No-store behavior is declared four ways at once: fetch({ cache: 'no-store' }), dynamic = 'force-dynamic', revalidate = 0 on every route, and fetchCache = 'force-no-store' in the layout — redundant belt-and-suspenders that adds migration surface when the segment configs are retired.
findings.suggestion: Pick one mechanism (the per-fetch cache: 'no-store' in lib/api.ts is already sufficient and is the most future-proof location) and drop the rest.

findings.issue: The home page ships the full 1,025-species index to the client for filtering with plain useState/useMemo; it solves the problem with long-stable primitives rather than anything new, which is the right call for stability but means the newest prefetching/instant-navigation improvements in Next 16.4 are not leveraged.
findings.suggestion: No action needed for this dimension; if bundle size matters, consider server-side filtering in a Route Handler — still fully stable APIs.

summary: This app contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs — no config flags, no unstable_/experimental_ names, no use cache, no PPR. Its whole surface is Link, Metadata, useRouter, React 19 stable hooks and route segment configs, pinned to the current stable Next 16.4.3. The only forward-looking risk is the inverse of experimentalness: it sits squarely on the 'previous' caching model that Next 16.4 is actively steering away from, so the real upgrade debt is at Next 17, not at the bleeding edge.
